findings.evidence: The theorem at line 139 uses `Matrix.of (fun i j ↦ extEuler ...)`; `rg "extEulerMatrix"` finds no ungraded declaration, while `ExtEuler/Graded/Matrix.lean` exports `gradedExtEulerMatrix`, `_apply`, `_of_of`, and `_basis_change`.
findings.fix: Define the ungraded `extEulerMatrix` in the general Ext-Euler matrix layer, add `[simp]` entry/object-class lemmas analogous to `gradedExtEulerMatrix_apply` and `gradedExtEulerMatrix_of_of`, and state this identity using it.
findings.issue: The public result repeatedly embeds the Ext-Euler matrix as an anonymous `Matrix.of`, so consumers cannot name it or use characteristic entry lemmas; this is inconsistent with the existing graded matrix API.

findings.evidence: Its statement mentions only `FiniteDimensional`, `ModuleCat.isFG`, `admitsFiniteResolution`, and `finiteProjectiveModules`; its proof uses the general `FiniteResolution.isEulerAdmissible` API already defined in `ExtEuler/Resolution.lean`.
findings.fix: Move it to `Algebra/Homology/EulerCharacteristic/ExtEuler/Resolution.lean` or a module-specific resolution file imported by this one.
findings.issue: `isEulerAdmissibleOn_isFG` is general finite-resolution infrastructure and does not depend on Cartan matrices, simples, or projective covers, so placing it in this representation-specific matrix module forces unrelated users to import that layer.

summary: The matrix result lacks a named Ext-Euler matrix API, and a general admissibility theorem is placed in the representation-specific file.
